I'm 64 years old, only finished primary school. I've worked my 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, same as my father. I don't read books about farming — I watch what my neighbors do, and I talk to the seed dealer when I buy inputs. I learned that if something worked last year and the year before, I should keep doing it. Changing is dangerous.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I ploughed deep before planting, and I put down base fertilizer — about 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer. I planted improved seed, not the old traditional kind. Now in spring, the wheat needs food. I will spread 20 kg of urea per mu for top dressing, and irrigate three times: the green-up water, the jointing water, and the grain-filling water. My well pump can handle all 10 mu. I will spray herbicide once and fungicide once. I want 520 kg per mu from that wheat. Last year I got about 500 kg, and I want to match that or do a little better.

After I harvest the wheat in June, I will rotary till the ground quick — there's no time to plough deep for the summer crop. I will plant hybrid maize seed, about 4 jin per mu. I will put 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu when I sow, then top dress with 25 kg of urea per mu when the plants are knee-high. That's about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu for the maize. I will irrigate three times in summer, and spray pesticide twice — once for weeds, once for bugs. I expect 600 kg per mu if the rain cooperates.

I think hard about money. A bag of urea is over 130 yuan now, compound fertilizer is 160 yuan. For both crops I need maybe 35 bags total. That's nearly 5,000 yuan. But I cannot cut back. My neighbor Wang tried to save 200 yuan on fertilizer two years ago and his wheat was so thin he lost half a harvest. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost I accept.
